title: A Painting of the Savanna
subtitle: This document, which can be read both as a map and a painting, was part of a legal proceeding that consolidated one of the most important haciendas and family lineages of the New Kingdom of Granada.

title: Villages for the "indios"
subtitle: The Spanish created laws to force Indigenous peoples to abandon their former settlements and live in grid-like villages (also called reducciones) organized around a main square and a church. The objective of the measure was to coerce Indigenous peoples into giving up their customs.

title: From Terraces to Grasslands
subtitle: Although we find animals like cows and horses on the map, these were not native to the New World, but were introduced with the conquest. The map shows the transformation of the Indigenous agricultural landscape into grasslands for cattle raising.

title: A Divided Landscape
subtitle: This painting was used as a legal document in order to prove a Spaniard’s ownership of a large estate in the Bogotá savanna. As Spanish legal procedures endorsed a Spaniard’s property ownership, Indigenous peoples were being dispossessed. Indigenous people were given a resguardo or reservation (a much smaller communal property which they were not allowed to sell) and were forced to work on estates. In this sense, this is a map of land dispossession and of the transformation of the Indigenous agricultural landscapes.
